findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] ProvideAnonymousDeviceService's signature changed from (usageStats, authBroker, anonStore anonstore.AnonStore, ...) to (..., sqlStore db.DB, ...), but the generated wire file (pkg/server/wire_gen.go, which is committed in this repo, not shown in the diff) still calls it with the old argument list, so the package fails to compile until wire is regenerated. Every CI build and local developer build breaks at compile time on the unchanged wire_gen.go call site (`ProvideAnonymousDeviceService(..., anonStore, ...)` passed as db.DB); the author must regenerate wire and include it in the PR.

[ADVISORY] ProvideAnonDBStore's signature gained a required deviceLimit int64 parameter, but the diff shows no update to the wire registration (pkg/server/wire_server.go) or any other out-of-tree call site that constructs the store, so any remaining caller using the old two-arg form fails to compile. The wire provider set still declares `wire.Bind(new(anonstore.AnonStore), new(*anonstore.AnonDBStore))` / ProvideAnonDBStore; while wire can inject cfg-derived values, the committed wire_gen.go calls ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore) with one argument and stops compiling; also the repo pattern of registering the store separately now double-constructs the store (once via wire, once inline in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService), so the API endpoints in api.go and the tagging path in impl.go use two independent AnonDBStore instances.

[BUG] AnonymousDeviceLimit is declared as `int64` with json tag `anonymousDeviceLimit` and no omitempty, so when the limit is unset (0, the ini default from setting.go:device_limit MustInt64(0)) the DTO serializes the number 0, while the frontend type `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200) and the runtime default `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` (packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97) both model unset as undefined. Any frontend consumer doing `config.anonymousDeviceLimit === undefined` to detect 'no limit configured' gets 0 instead, and consumers treating 0 as a usable limit (limit of zero devices) behave as if anonymous access is fully device-blocked; the two representations of 'unset' diverge across the process boundary.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice was moved from a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout onto the synchronous request path using the request-scoped context, so every anonymous authentication now performs the DB count (CountDevices) plus update/insert inline, and inherits the HTTP request's cancellation/lifetime instead of an independent one. Anonymous users on slow DBs see their login latency grow by the anon-device query round trips, and a request cancellation aborts the device tag mid-transaction where it previously completed; also the recover() guard is gone, so a panic inside TagDevice now propagates out of Authenticate and takes down the request handler (previously logged as a warning).

[ADVISORY] The device-limit check (SELECT CountDevices) and the subsequent insert/update run as separate statements without a transaction or row lock, so the limit is enforced on a count taken before the write rather than atomically at the write. Under concurrent first-time anonymous requests with deviceLimit=N, N+ devices are inserted because each request counts N-1 rows before any peer commits; operators who set the limit as a hard cap for licensing get over-limit device rows, and the updateDevice fallback then rejects legitimate returning devices whose rows exist.

[ADVISORY] anonymousDeviceLimit is added to the frontend GrafanaConfig surface but no code anywhere in the diff reads it, so the value crosses into every browser page with zero consumers. The frontend half of this change is inert: backend settings expose the limit but no UI can surface 'device limit reached' to anonymous users, so when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the anonymous user gets only a generic auth failure with no explanation of the configured cap.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE clause requires updated_at BETWEEN (UpdatedAt-30d) AND (UpdatedAt+1min), so a device that exists but whose stored updated_at is older than 30 days yields rowsAffected==0 and is reported as ErrDeviceLimitReached even though it is a returning, under-limit device. An anonymous user returning after a 30-day absence during a full device table (limit reached) gets ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of having their device row refreshed, permanently locking them out until the nightly DeleteDevicesOlderThan cleanup runs.

[BUG] Authenticate returns the raw anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached to the authn broker, surfacing an internal store error to the anonymous request instead of a defined auth outcome. When device limit is hit, the anonymous client returns a non-nil error that authn treats as an authentication failure (likely a 500/internal error response), not a deliberate 'device rejected' 4xx; every anonymous request from a blocked device sees an opaque server error, and no test covers this client-level path.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a non-atomic CountDevices-then-insert sequence, so concurrent requests exceed the configured device limit. N simultaneous anonymous requests against an empty table with device_limit=1 all observe count < 1 and all insert, permanently exceeding the limit; the check provides no guarantee under Grafana's concurrent request load.

[BUG] updateDevice conflates 'device not updated within the window' with 'device limit reached', rejecting known devices on MySQL when the UPDATE is a no-op. On MySQL, RowsAffected is 0 when the new values equal the existing ones: with the limit reached, a returning device whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at are identical at timestamp precision gets ErrDeviceLimitReached and is blocked despite being a known device; similarly a device last seen just over 30 days ago (updated_at outside the BETWEEN window) is blocked instead of expiring/being re-created.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice was moved from a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout onto the synchronous authentication path, and the panic recovery was removed. Every anonymous request now performs an inline DB read+write before a response is produced: a slow or contended database adds latency to all anonymous auth (hot-path regression), a canceled request context aborts tagging that previously always completed, and a panic inside TagDevice now takes down the request handler instead of being logged and swallowed.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only exercises the store's limit rejection; no test covers the client/authn behavior, the returning-device update path, or limit boundary (count == limit vs count > limit). The most user-visible new behavior — an anonymous request being rejected at the authn layer with ErrDeviceLimitReached (client.go:45-47) — has zero coverage, so a regression that turns this into a swallowed log line or a hard 500 ships undetected; the test also never verifies that an already-known device still updates successfully when the limit is reached.

[ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is declared as a non-pointer int64 serialized unconditionally, while the frontend types declare it number | undefined, and no frontend code in the diff consumes the value. The frontend settings payload always carries anonymousDeviceLimit (including 0), contradicting the optional TS type, and the field is shipped to the browser with no reader anywhere in the diff — operators configuring device_limit get no UI feedback and the payload contract between Go DTO and TS type silently drifts.

[BUG] TagDevice was moved from an async, timeout-guarded goroutine onto the synchronous authentication path, so every anonymous request now blocks on a DB write and any transient DB error escalates from a logged warning to an authentication failure. The removed code ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and swallowed all errors; the new code awaits it inline and returns the error to authn, so a slow or failed anon_device write (or updateDevice error) makes every anonymous login fail and adds DB round-trip latency (plus the added COUNT query when device_limit>0) to the hot auth path — the stated requirement was only a device limit, not turning tagging into an auth gate.

[BUG] The device limit is enforced with a non-atomic COUNT-then-INSERT sequence, so the configured limit is not actually enforced under concurrent requests. Two anonymous clients arriving concurrently when count == limit-1 both pass the count check and both insert/upsert, exceeding the configured device_limit; the invariant this PR exists to enforce (at most N devices) is violated by a simple race, and once exceeded the limit can never shrink because updates-only mode keeps the extra rows.

[ADVISORY] The PR plumbs anonymousDeviceLimit through the entire frontend settings surface (GrafanaConfig type, GrafanaBootConfig, FrontendSettingsDTO, getFrontendSettings) with no frontend consumer anywhere in the diff. This is implementation work not traceable to the stated requirement (a server-side device limit); it ships an inert config field to every browser. Operators reading the settings DTO may assume the limit is frontend-enforced or configurable client-side; if no UI follows, the DTO field and TS types are dead weight that must be maintained across refactors. Either the consuming UI belongs in this PR or the frontend plumbing should be deleted.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE updated_at BETWEEN (now-30d) AND (now+1min) clause conflates 'device limit reached' with 'device record stale', returning ErrDeviceLimitReached for a returning device whose last update is older than 30 days. A device absent for 31 days (thus not counted in the limit window) that returns when the limit is full fails the BETWEEN predicate, and the client in client.go translates ErrDeviceLimitReached into an auth rejection with a misleading 'device limit reached' error, when semantically it is an expired-device case that should be treated as a fresh insert occupying a real slot. The client has no way to distinguish these and the log/API surfaces the wrong cause.

[ADVISORY] The added CountDevices call runs on every CreateOrUpdateDevice when device_limit > 0, adding an unconditional full-window COUNT query to the per-request anonymous tagging path that previously issued only a single upsert. On high-traffic anonymous deployments, every request now pays a COUNT over 30 days of anon_device rows (index scan on updated_at window) plus the upsert, doubling the write-path DB cost of anonymous auth; a reviewer should confirm the count query is indexed or hoisted behind the local cache added in impl.go.

[BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a check-then-insert (CountDevices followed by a separate INSERT) with no transaction, unique constraint, or atomic guard, so the limit is not actually enforced under concurrency. Under a burst of concurrent anonymous requests, every request reads count < limit and inserts, so the device count exceeds AnonymousDeviceLimit by as much as the number of concurrent requests; operators who set device_limit=N see more than N devices, defeating the feature's contract.

[BUG] updateDevice conflates 'the device does not exist (or its updated_at is outside the 30-day window)' with 'device limit reached' by treating rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. An anonymous device whose row exists but whose updated_at is older than anonymousDeviceExpiration (e.g. a device returning after >30 days, whose row has not yet been purged by the cleanup job) falls into the limit-reached branch, the UPDATE matches no rows, and the user gets a device-limit auth error even when the count check would have admitted them; the same path also returns the misleading error for any genuinely new device, so callers cannot distinguish 'blocked' from 'stale-but-valid'.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice moved from an async goroutine with a 2-minute timeout to a synchronous call on the anonymous authentication path, adding per-request DB round trips (a COUNT plus an INSERT/UPDATE when device_limit>0) with no timeout or degradation. Every anonymous request now pays DB latency inline; when the database is slow or down, anonymous page loads stall or fail on the count query instead of degrading to fire-and-forget tagging as before — a hot-path regression and cascading-failure path with no fallback.

[ADVISORY] When device_limit>0, every tagged anonymous request issues CountDevices over a 30-day updated_at range, which is a full-table scan unless an index on anon_device.updated_at exists. On high-traffic anonymous deployments the count runs per request (cache miss) and scans the whole growing anon_device table each time; operators enabling device_limit see a linear-in-table-size query cost multiplied by request rate.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice changed from swallowing tagDeviceUI errors (log-and-continue) to returning them, a sentinel-meaning change with no audit of other callers besides the authn client. Any caller of TagDevice outside client.go (or added later) that previously relied on best-effort semantics now fails on transient DB errors even when the operator has not set a device limit, turning a non-critical analytics write into a request-failing operation; the client.go path handles only ErrDeviceLimitReached specially and other callers get raw errors.

[ADVISORY] The Go DTO always serializes anonymousDeviceLimit as an int64 (no omitempty, zero when unset) while the frontend contract declares number | undefined, so the two copies of the shape already disagree. Frontend consumers checking `config.anonymousDeviceLimit === undefined` to detect 'feature not configured' never see undefined — they see 0 — so any future code distinguishing 'disabled' from 'limit of zero' silently misbehaves, and the client/server schema copies drift from day one.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE clause uses a bare time.Minute fudge added to the device's own client-supplied-timestamp-derived UpdatedAt (rather than server time) as the upper window bound, an unexplained dimensioned magic number whose correctness depends on clock alignment between the timestamp writer and this query. If TagDevice ever sets UpdatedAt from a skewed source (or a future code path passes an older UpdatedAt), the +1-minute bound silently stops matching and every returning device is misclassified as over-limit; the unit/provenance of the fudge is unreviewable, so the next editor can widen or drop it without any test catching the change.

[BUG] Removing the fire-and-forget goroutine and returning ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate converts anonymous device tagging from best-effort telemetry into a hard authentication gate, so hitting the device limit rejects anonymous users from Grafana entirely instead of just skipping the tag. An operator who sets device_limit sees every new anonymous session (and every existing device with stale updated_at) fail authentication with an error propagated out of the authn client — previously the same store failure was logged as a warning and access continued. This changes the objective from 'limit tracked devices' to 'deny anonymous access at the limit' without any indication the reviewer accepted that semantic shift.

[ADVISORY] Tagging was deliberately made asynchronous (with panic recovery and a 2-minute timeout) to keep it off the auth critical path; this diff makes it synchronous on the request context and deletes the recover() guard and timeout. Every anonymous request now performs at least one synchronous COUNT query plus an INSERT/UPDATE before the identity is returned, adding DB latency to the anonymous login hot path; the removed timeout also means a hung DB connection now stalls the request instead of a background goroutine. Who gets bitten: any deployment with anonymous access enabled under load.

[BUG] updateDevice conflates 'device not found or not updated within the 30-day window' with 'device limit reached' by returning ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever rowsAffected == 0, so a known returning device whose last update is older than 30 days is rejected as if it were a new device. A loyal anonymous user returning after a 31-day absence gets an authentication error (via the new return path in client.go) even though their device already exists in the table and consuming no new slot — the diff's own test only covers the fresh-device case, so this regression ships silently.

[ADVISORY] The limit check (SELECT COUNT) and the subsequent INSERT are two separate non-transactional statements, so N concurrent requests at count == limit-1 all pass the check and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. Under concurrent load the device count exceeds AnonymousDeviceLimit by up to (concurrency-1) rows per burst; operators relying on the limit as a hard cap get silently violated bounds.

[ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is added to the frontend settings payload and the GrafanaConfig type, but nothing in this diff (frontend or backend) reads anonymousDeviceLimit from the config. The field crosses the process boundary into every browser session with zero consumers — dead public API surface that must now be maintained for compatibility; if frontend consumption was the accepted intent, it did not ship in this PR.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice now propagates the tagDeviceUI error to all callers after it was previously logged-and-swallowed, which also changes behavior for the non-UI tagging paths and any future PostLoginHook usage, not just the new device-limit flow. Any transient store error in tagDeviceUI (previously a debug log) now bubbles up to Authenticate and, per client.go, only ErrDeviceLimitReached is fatal today, but any new caller of TagDevice inherits fail-closed semantics; the change in error contract is broader than the device-limit intent.

[BUG] The device-limit check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is a non-atomic count-then-act sequence, so the limit is bypassable under concurrent anonymous requests. CountDevices and the subsequent insert run in separate sessions with no locking; N concurrent requests all read count < limit and all insert, so an attacker (or natural burst of anonymous traffic) exceeds cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit by an arbitrary amount — the enforcement the feature promises silently fails exactly under load.

[ADVISORY] An unauthenticated party can deliberately exhaust the device quota to deny anonymous access to all new visitors. Any anonymous client (no credentials required) can mint device IDs up to the configured limit; once the table holds `device_limit` rows updated within the 30-day window, every request from a device not already in the table returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, and client.go returns that error from Authenticate — a trivial, unauthenticated denial-of-service against the anonymous access service that operators will experience as 'anonymous login broken' for 30 days unless they raise the limit or purge the table.

[ADVISORY] When deviceLimit > 0, every tagged anonymous request now issues an extra unconditional COUNT query (plus the update/insert) on the hot authentication path, replacing the previous fire-and-forget goroutine. Operators who set a device limit on a high-traffic anonymous deployment add a synchronous COUNT over the anon_device table (scanning rows within the 30-day window) to every anonymous request; on MySQL/Postgres without a covering index on updated_at this is a table-scan per request, a self-inflicted load/DoS amplifier the config knob does not warn about.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice is now executed synchronously in Authenticate with the request context, and the panic-recovery the old goroutine provided was removed, so a storage-layer panic in TagDevice now takes down the request instead of being logged. The previous code wrapped TagDevice in a goroutine with an explicit recover() (the authors clearly expected panics there); the replacement calls it inline in the auth path with no recover, so a driver-level panic during tagging crashes the anonymous authentication request — availability regression relative to the code being replaced.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit exercises only the failure sentinel of the new updateDevice path and never tests the success branch (rowsAffected > 0, i.e. an existing device within the 30-day window is actually updated when the limit is reached). A regression in the UPDATE statement's WHERE clause (e.g. wrong time-window bounds causing every update of a legitimate returning device to return 0 rows and ErrDeviceLimitReached) would lock out all anonymous devices past the limit while every existing test still passes; operators with device_limit configured get repeat anonymous users rejected as new-device-joins with no test catching it.

[ADVISORY] The new error-propagation branch in TagDevice (impl.go line ~147, `return err` after tagDeviceUI failure) has no test that triggers it — every case in TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag uses valid requests and require.NoError, which was the correct assertion only under the old swallow-and-log contract. The changed contract — TagDevice errors now propagate to Anonymous.Authenticate and reject authentication (client.go) instead of being logged — is verified by no test in the diff; a future refactor reverting the `return err` (restoring the silent swallow) passes the whole suite, and the device-limit rejection feature becomes a silent no-op for the UI path.

[ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit mutates and reuses the same Device pointer across both CreateOrUpdateDevice calls without asserting the first insert's stored state (no ListDevices/field assertions after the first call), so the test proves only that the second call errors, not that the limit logic was what caused it. If the pre-insert CountDevices query were broken (e.g. always returning a count >= limit, making every first-time create fall through to updateDevice and fail), the first require.NoError in this test would catch it, but a subtle off-by-one in the window bounds that only miscounts at boundaries escapes detection; checked database_test.go and impl_test.go — neither asserts stored device contents under a non-zero limit.

[BUG] The device limit is enforced with a check-then-act race: CountDevices and the subsequent insert/update run in separate statements with no unique constraint, transaction, or lock, so concurrent anonymous requests all read count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured device_limit. Under concurrent load the limit is silently bypassed: an operator setting device_limit = N gets many more than N tracked devices, defeating the feature's guarantee; the count also grows monotonically afterward, so the update-only fallback never triggers and no error surfaces.

[BUG] updateDevice treats RowsAffected()==0 as 'device limit reached', but on MySQL a matched row whose values are unchanged reports 0 affected rows (no clientFoundRows), so a returning device within the expiration window whose client_ip/user_agent/updated_at already equal the new values is falsely rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached. Once the limit is reached, a legitimate existing anonymous device making a request with identical IP/user-agent within the same timestamp gets its authentication rejected with the device-limit error instead of being served, on any MySQL-backed deployment.

[BUG] Returning ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate makes any new anonymous device (a device_id not already in the table) fail authentication entirely, so anonymous users are locked out of Grafana rather than merely not being tracked once the configured device limit is reached. An operator setting auth.anonymous device_limit = 100 gets a hard denial-of-service for all anonymous visitors after the 100th distinct device, with the raw 'device limit reached' error surfaced through the authn pipeline (500-class response) instead of the dashboard being served anonymously; rolling back the config requires a restart and there is no path to re-admit devices other than waiting 30 days for expiration/cleanup.

[BUG] updateDevice's WHERE clause (updated_at BETWEEN updated-30d AND updated+1min) cannot match rows older than 30 days, so when the limit is reached and an existing device's row is stale (cleanup job not yet run), the update affects 0 rows and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached — the row can neither be updated nor re-inserted. A single expired-but-not-yet-deleted row (device_limit = 1 case demonstrated in the new test with a shifted UpdatedAt) permanently blocks that device from authenticating until the DeleteDevicesOlderThan cleanup happens to run; if the anonymous cleanup job is disabled, the block never lifts.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice moved from a fire-and-forget background goroutine (previous code) to the synchronous authentication path, adding a COUNT over anon_device plus an UPDATE/INSERT to every uncached anonymous auth request. Every anonymous request not served by the 29-minute local cache now pays two synchronous DB round-trips in the auth critical path, and any transient DB error that was previously swallowed (Warn log) now fails the request; high-traffic public Grafana instances see added latency and a new hard dependency of anonymous auth on DB availability.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice's tagDeviceUI error was previously only logged (a.log.Debug) and TagDevice returned nil; the diff changes it to propagate the error, so any DB hiccup during tagging now bubbles up through Authenticate and rejects otherwise valid anonymous requests. Anonymous access availability is now coupled to a write to the anon_device tracking table — a table that is pure telemetry; a brief DB outage or lock contention on that table turns into anonymous login failures rather than degraded device statistics.

[ADVISORY] The device-limit check is a non-atomic count-then-write: CountDevices runs in one statement and the insert/update in another, so concurrent requests interleave and the limit is not actually enforced under load. A burst of concurrent anonymous requests each observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, letting the device count exceed the configured cap with no error anywhere; operators relying on the limit are silently misled. The strongest counter-argument is that this is a soft limit and approximate enforcement is acceptable, but the stored count then feeds future decisions and permanently drifts above the limit, so the soft-limit defense only holds if drift is bounded, which it is not.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout to a synchronous call on the auth request path using the request context, adding a COUNT over the 30-day anon_device window plus an UPSERT to every anonymous request that misses the local cache. Every uncached anonymous login now pays DB round-trips inline: with device_limit > 0 the CountDevices query runs on every cache miss, so DB latency or a slow anon_device table directly delays anonymous page loads; previously only the response lagged and the tag was eventually recorded. The counter-argument is that the local cache absorbs repeats, but first-hit and 29-minute-expiry requests still hit the DB synchronously, and with device_limit configured the count query is unconditional on that path.

[ADVISORY] updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any rowsAffected == 0, including the case where the device row exists but its updated_at falls outside the BETWEEN (t-30d, t+1min) window, so the error text misdescribes the actual condition (stale device, not limit exhaustion). An operator debugging 'device limit reached' errors from the anonymous auth path cannot distinguish a genuinely exhausted limit from a user presenting an expired (>30-day-old) device cookie; the deny outcome is the same but the error content misdirects debugging of the rate-limit/retention interaction.

[ADVISORY] AnonymousDeviceLimit is serialized as an always-present int64 (0 when unset) while the frontend contract GrafanaConfig.anonymousDeviceLimit is typed `number | undefined`, and GrafanaBootConfig initializes it to undefined, so the wire value and the client-side type/domain disagree. Frontend code that follows the declared type and branches on `anonymousDeviceLimit` truthiness or undefined to detect 'no limit configured' will treat a configured limit of... actually 0 means unset server-side too, but any consumer reading the type expects undefined for unset and receives 0, and a limit configured to a truthy-but-low value vs absent cannot be distinguished the way the type promises, leading to dead `undefined` branches in the frontend.

[ADVISORY] TagDevice now propagates tagDeviceUI errors to the caller (return err) instead of only logging them, and the Anonymous auth client returns ErrDeviceLimitReached as a hard authentication failure, so a store-side condition during device tagging converts what was previously a successful anonymous login into a rejected request. When the device limit is reached, anonymous users with no prior device row receive an auth error instead of service; combined with the count-then-update race this failure mode is reachable even for devices that were just created moments earlier. The counter-argument is that denying new devices is the feature's intent, but the same error also fires for existing rows outside the updated_at window (see updateDevice finding), so real users get rejected where the feature intends only new-device denial.

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

Since `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `updateDevice` specifically when the limit is reached, this conflates “cannot update due to matching/window/no-op” with “limit reached” and can incorrectly reject a known device instead of expiring/recreating or treating it as updated.

The panic-recovery removal is also verifiable (the `defer recover` block was deleted), but whether an upstream middleware recovers panics is not shown, so “takes down the request handler” is a plausible risk rather than a guaranteed defect. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only exercises the store's limit rejection; no test covers the client/authn behavior, the returning-device update path, or limit boundary (count == limit vs count > limit). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TagDevice was moved from an async, timeout-guarded goroutine onto the synchronous authentication path, so every anonymous request now blocks on a DB write and any transient DB error escalates from a logged warning to an authentication failure. The removed code ran TagDevice in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and swallowed all errors; the new code awaits it inline and returns the error to authn, so a slow or failed anon_device write (or updateDevice error) makes every anonymous login fail and adds DB round-trip latency (plus the added COUNT query when device_limit>0) to the hot auth path — the stated requirement was only a device limit, not turning tagging into an auth gate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move tagging onto the synchronous auth path: `Anonymous.Authenticate` removes the goroutine/timeout and now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). That can add latency to the hot authentication path and, when `AnonymousDeviceLimit>0`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` now does an extra `CountDevices` query and may run an `UPDATE` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The device limit is enforced with a non-atomic COUNT-then-INSERT sequence, so the configured limit is not actually enforced under concurrent requests. Two anonymous clients arriving concurrently when count == limit-1 both pass the count check and both insert/upsert, exceeding the configured device_limit; the invariant this PR exists to enforce (at most N devices) is violated by a simple race, and once exceeded the limit can never shrink because updates-only mode keeps the extra rows.

adjudication.rationale: In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, enforcement is implemented as `CountDevices(...)` followed by an insert/upsert path when `count < s.deviceLimit`. This check and the subsequent insert/upsert are not performed atomically (no shared transaction/locking across the count and the write), so concurrent requests can both observe `count == limit-1` and both proceed to create, exceeding `deviceLimit` despite it being configured. The diff shows the COUNT-then-write sequence and no concurrency control around it, so the limit is not strictly enforced under contention.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] updateDevice's WHERE updated_at BETWEEN (now-30d) AND (now+1min) clause conflates 'device limit reached' with 'device record stale', returning ErrDeviceLimitReached for a returning device whose last update is older than 30 days. A device absent for 31 days (thus not counted in the limit window) that returns when the limit is full fails the BETWEEN predicate, and the client in client.go translates ErrDeviceLimitReached into an auth rejection with a misleading 'device limit reached' error, when semantically it is an expired-device case that should be treated as a fresh insert occupying a real slot. AND ?` (with bounds computed from `device.UpdatedAt`), and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `RowsAffected()==0`. When `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is in the `count >= s.deviceLimit` branch, a device record that exists but has `updated_at` older than the 30-day window will fail the `BETWEEN` predicate, yield 0 affected rows, and be reported as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. `client.go` then treats `ErrDeviceLimitReached` specially by returning it (auth rejection). This does conflate “no matching row due to staleness/missing record” with “limit reached” at the error-reporting level, making the surfaced reason ambiguous/misleading. However, the diff alone doesn’t establish the intended product semantics (whether a >30d-stale device should be allowed to re-register when the limit is full), so it’s more an edge-case/semantics concern than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The added CountDevices call runs on every CreateOrUpdateDevice when device_limit > 0, adding an unconditional full-window COUNT query to the per-request anonymous tagging path that previously issued only a single upsert. On high-traffic anonymous deployments, every request now pays a COUNT over 30 days of anon_device rows (index scan on updated_at window) plus the upsert, doubling the write-path DB cost of anonymous auth; a reviewer should confirm the count query is indexed or hoisted behind the local cache added in impl.go.

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` now executes `s.CountDevices(...)` on every call when `s.deviceLimit > 0` (before the upsert logic). This is an additional DB query over a 30-day `updated_at` window (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) that did not exist previously, so it can increase per-tagging DB load in anonymous-heavy setups. The diff does not show any indexing/optimization or caching around this count at the store level; the existing service-level local cache may reduce calls, but the count still runs for every uncached tag. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the device limit with a check-then-insert (CountDevices followed by a separate INSERT) with no transaction, unique constraint, or atomic guard, so the limit is not actually enforced under concurrency. Under a burst of concurrent anonymous requests, every request reads count < limit and inserts, so the device count exceeds AnonymousDeviceLimit by as much as the number of concurrent requests; operators who set device_limit=N see more than N devices, defeating the feature's contract.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the limit is enforced via a non-atomic sequence: it calls `CountDevices(...)` and, only if `count >= s.deviceLimit`, it switches to `updateDevice`; otherwise it proceeds to insert/upsert. This check-then-write occurs without any transaction/locking shown in the diff, so concurrent callers can all observe `count < limit` and each insert, exceeding `deviceLimit` under load. The diff does not show any other atomic guard around this path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateDevice conflates 'the device does not exist (or its updated_at is outside the 30-day window)' with 'device limit reached' by treating rowsAffected==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached. An anonymous device whose row exists but whose updated_at is older than anonymousDeviceExpiration (e.g. a device returning after >30 days, whose row has not yet been purged by the cleanup job) falls into the limit-reached branch, the UPDATE matches no rows, and the user gets a device-limit auth error even when the count check would have admitted them; the same path also returns the misleading error for any genuinely new device, so callers cannot distinguish 'blocked' from 'stale-but-valid'.

In that situation, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when the UPDATE affects 0 rows (device_id missing or `updated_at` outside the 30-day window) does not contradict the preceding count check—the count check would *not* have “admitted them” because it already determined the limit was reached. AND ?` using bounds derived from `device.UpdatedAt` (`device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration)` to `device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(time.Minute)`). For a new `device_id` (not already in `anon_device`), the UPDATE affects 0 rows, so once the limit is reached, new anonymous visitors will hit `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and be denied authentication rather than simply not being tracked.
